Device GUI pages and their layouts

How SATOM draws a device's own GUI pages when the fleet mixes firmware builds - where each layout comes from, the three page states, the marks on fields and what a failed read says.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsprotection.view
📍 WhereFortiWeb, FortiGate, FortiADC ADOM → the product's group in the device menu → any page (URL /workspace/<id>/fwgui/<page>)
On this page
  • What is it?
  • The layout-origin sentence
  • The three page states
  • Fields when the layout is from another build
  • Dialogs and tabs the device handles itself
  • When a read fails
  • FortiWeb with ADOMs enabled
  • Troubleshooting
  • The banner says "layout from an older train" on a page I need
  • A page is missing from the menu but its address opens
  • A control says "not bound to a field" or a column says "not bound"
  • A dropdown is a text box marked "choices not measured"

What is it?#

A device's menu pages (Server Objects, Policy, Network and the rest) are drawn from layouts that were measured on real firmware builds and arrive with the knowledge packs. A fleet rarely runs one build, so the layout SATOM draws for a device may have been measured on another build. Every page says where its layout comes from, and what that means for the page.

The layout-origin sentence#

The banner at the top of every list, dialog, Not in GUI, but in CLI section, the Not in GUI device page and the exception forms reads the same way:

Layout measured on FortiWeb 8.0.6 build0116 · this device runs 8.0.8 build0140 · same train

Both builds are zero padded exactly as the device reports them. The badge at the end says how close the two are:

Badge Colour Meaning
same build green The layout was measured on this exact build. Nothing else is said.
same version / same train blue The closest layout of the same version or train. Fields the device has and the layout does not place are listed under Not in GUI, but in CLI.
layout from an older train yellow The device runs a newer train than any layout. Fields the newer build adds are not drawn from the layout; the ones the device has are listed under Not in GUI, but in CLI.
layout from a newer train yellow The device runs an older train than any layout. Some fields shown may not exist on this firmware.
firmware not read yet / The firmware of this device is not known yet yellow The layout was chosen by the model on the device record. Run a firmware check, or wait for the hourly device sync.

A knowledge pack badge beside it means the layout came from an imported knowledge pack. The same sentence and badges are used for FortiWeb, FortiGate and FortiADC pages.

The three page states#

SATOM decides from the API library of the device's exact build whether a page exists there. The menu, the page, its banner and the build diff all read that one answer.

State What you see
On this build The page works normally.
Not on this build (measured) The build was measured and the object is not there (for example MCP on 7.6.8, or File Exception on 8.0.8). The page is left out of the menu. Its address still answers, read-only, with a grey not on this build badge in the origin line: FortiWeb 7.6.8 does not have this object (measured). The page exists from 8.0.5 on. (or The page was removed after 7.6.8.), with no Create New, no Save and no "+ Create" from a selector. The page says it once: the statement and an empty list (Nothing to list on this build.), with no older/newer-train warning above it and no second copy of the sentence. The origin line above (Layout measured on FortiWeb 7.6.8 …) still names the layout the page would have drawn.
Not measured on this build yet The library never measured the object on this build. The page stays in the menu and works; it may not apply.

A page the device shows under two names across builds (Let's Encrypt and ACME, Mobile API, OCSP, Web Anti-Defacement) appears once in the menu: the name whose layout was measured closest to the device's build. The other name is not a second editor: both names edit the same collections, so opening the other name's address redirects to the page of the device's own build, with one flash. The flash says "Let's Encrypt" is called "ACME" on fwb-01 when the two names differ, and This address is the other build's name for "OCSP" when the object carries one title on both builds and only the page address differs. There is no "Open it" note and no Create New on the old address. Writes are not redirected.

Fields when the layout is from another build#

  • A choice list the layout lost (a drop-down, a radio group or a set of checkboxes) is filled from the device's own build in the API library. Failing that, from the same field in the nearest other layout, marked options from 7.6.8, not verified on 8.0.8. Only with neither is it a text box, marked choices not measured. That mark appears only on a choice control that has a field.
  • A select that is a reference to another table (HA SDN Connector, a server pool member's SDN Connector, a Site Publish rule's RADIUS Server: the build's CLI tree types them as the name of another table's row) is a reference selector listing that table, not a text box, even when the layout lost its source. The 8.0.8 Content Routing match dialog takes its choices from its match-list table.
  • A control the layout draws with no field says not bound to a field: SATOM draws no value and saves nothing from it (FortiGate Security Fabric Management IP/FQDN and Management port). A tab with no caption takes the title of the dialog it opens.
  • A field the device's build lacks is drawn disabled with not on 8.0.8, and (renamed to h2-setting-initial-window-size) when the library knows the rename.
  • A field the build was never measured on keeps working and carries not measured on 8.0.8.
  • The HTTP Protocol Constraints table (drawn by hand, one row per constraint) carries the same marks when its layout comes from another build: a constraint the build lacks is drawn disabled with not on 8.0.8 (renamed to h2-setting-initial-window-size-check), one nobody measured says not measured on 8.0.8.
  • A list column the layout does not bind to a field of the rows (FortiWeb Network > Interface on 7.6.8: Members, IPv4, IPv4 Access Options, Status and Link Status; on 8.0.8 only Members and Link Status) carries a not bound tag on its header, and its cells read n/a, so an empty cell is never read as "no IP address". On 8.0.8 the Interface list shows the IPv4 address, the access options and the status.
  • A dialog the layout draws with fewer fields than the object has gets the missing REST fields in a last block, Not in this layout (REST fields) (see Exceptions).

These marks are display only: what Save sends is decided by the build check.

Dialogs and tabs the device handles itself#

Some parts of a device's menu are not configuration objects SATOM can write. SATOM draws them from the layout so the page reads like the device, and says what it will not do:

  • An import dialog (Sign CA, Scanner Integration > Scanner File Import) is drawn read-only, with no Save and no "creates the object" line: Import is done on the device: SATOM does not upload files through this dialog. The fields below are what the device's dialog shows. Where SATOM has its own flow for the same job, the sentence ends with a link to it: on Sign CA that is SATOM has its own import for this object: Import, which opens the certificate import.
  • A tab the device manages (System > Maintenance > Firmware, first tab) shows one sentence instead of a list: Managed on the device: edits this page through its own GUI calls, which SATOM never replays. SATOM draws its layout read-only; nothing is sent from it. It links to SATOM's own flow, here Upgrade Flow. The second tab, Automatic Patch Upgrades, is an ordinary settings form with Save.
  • A monitor tab (API Protection > ML Based API Protection: Overview, API Path, Tree View, API View, Event Log) shows A monitor view of the device: nothing to configure here. No toolbar and no grid are drawn.
  • A settings form offers Save only when its object was read from the device and SATOM may write it. An object that could not be read, or that SATOM does not write, is drawn read-only with no Save.
  • A dialog the template does not title is named by the entry that opens it, else by the page name with (new) or (edit) (for example ML Based API Protection (new)). A raw template id is never the title.

When a read fails#

A form or list whose live read fails says what happened with one wording on every product (FortiWeb, FortiGate, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator):

Sentence Case
fwb-01 is unreachable Nothing answered.
fwb-01 does not serve this object over REST The library says the build lacks the object.
adc-01 refused the read: HTTP 200, Invalid VM License The device answered and said no; the sentence carries its status, code and message (for example HTTP 500, errcode -20001, The REST API has invalid URL).

FortiWeb with ADOMs enabled#

A row registered with no ADOM shows the root ADOM only. When the device has ADOMs enabled, its empty lists and its Capacity counts say so: ADOMs are enabled on this device: this row shows the root ADOM only. The objects of the other ADOMs belong to rows of their own …, instead of suggesting a configuration sync. To see another ADOM's objects, register the same host again with ADOM (vdom) set to that ADOM's name (Appliances); the device then has one row per ADOM.

Troubleshooting#

The banner says "layout from an older train" on a page I need#

The device runs a train newer than any measured layout. The fields the layout does not draw are in Not in GUI, but in CLI at the bottom of the dialog, and editable there. Importing a newer knowledge pack removes the warning.

A page is missing from the menu but its address opens#

The page's object was measured as not served on this build. See the page state above; the page is read-only on purpose.

A control says "not bound to a field" or a column says "not bound"#

The measured layout draws the control or the column but does not say which field it shows. SATOM draws no value for it and saves nothing from it; the field itself, when the device has it, is in Not in GUI, but in CLI. A newer knowledge pack for that build usually binds it.

A dropdown is a text box marked "choices not measured"#

Neither the device's own build nor any other layout has the list of choices. Harvest or import that build (Schema builds).

#gui layout#layout measured#same build#older train#newer train#knowledge pack#page state#read-only page#not measured#choices not measured#adom enabled#firmware build
